title: How do you implement tiered retries for transient failures using retry topics (main -> `retry.1s` -> `retry.5s` -> `retry.30s` -> DLQ, graduating a message to the next topic each time it fails) instead of blocking the main consumer, and why use exponential backoff + jitter (to avoid a thundering-herd retry storm) while classifying transient (retry) vs permanent (straight to DLQ) failures?
shortTitle: Tiered retries with retry topics, exponential backoff with jitter, and transient vs permanent classification
keyPoints: Blocking retries on the main consumer stall the whole partition; retry topics move waiting off the main path.
Tiers form a graduating ladder (main -> retry.1s -> retry.5s -> retry.30s -> DLQ) with increasing delays.
Exponential backoff gives a failing dependency time to recover without hammering it immediately.
Jitter adds random spread to delays so correlated failures do not create a thundering-herd retry storm.
Transient failures (timeout, 503) enter the retry ladder; permanent failures (validation, deser) go straight to DLQ.
Spring Kafka @RetryableTopic auto-creates retry and DLT topics with configurable attempts and backoff.
Ordering is relaxed because a retried record arrives later than its neighbors.

s1_definition.oneliner: Graduate transient failures through delayed retry topics with exponential backoff plus jitter so the main consumer never blocks, and send permanent failures straight to the dead letter queue.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Tiered retry topics** -- a non-blocking retry pattern where a failed record is republished to dedicated retry topics with increasing delays instead of blocking the main consumer.
- **Retry ladder** -- the graduating chain of topics: main -> retry.1s -> retry.5s -> retry.30s -> DLQ, with each tier adding a longer delay.
- **Exponential backoff** -- delays that grow geometrically (1s, 5s, 30s) to give a failing dependency time to recover.
- **Jitter** -- a random spread added to each delay to prevent a thundering-herd storm when many records fail at the same instant.
- **Failure classification** -- separating transient failures (worth retrying) from permanent failures (straight to DLQ without wasting tiers).
- **@RetryableTopic** -- a Spring Kafka annotation that auto-creates retry and DLT topics with configurable attempts, backoff multiplier, and exception exclusions.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India's settlement desk hitting a temporary outage in the credit bureau. Instead of the clerk freezing on one form while the bureau is down, the form is dropped into a try again in 1 second tray, then a try again in 5 seconds tray, then a try again in 30 seconds tray, each handled by a different clerk who only picks up forms after the delay. If it still fails, it goes to the problem tray. Jitter is like telling clerks not to all retry at the exact same tick, so they do not stampede the bureau the moment it recovers.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Tiered Retry Flow

  ┌──────────────┐
  │ transfers    │  FAIL (transient)
  │ (main topic) │──────────┐
  └──────────────┘          │
       │ commit              ▼
       │              ┌──────────────┐
       │              │ retry-1s     │  FAIL
       │              │ (wait 1s)    │──────────┐
       │              └──────────────┘          │
       │                                        ▼
       │                                 ┌──────────────┐
       │                                 │ retry-5s     │  FAIL
       │                                 │ (wait 5s)    │──────┐
       │                                 └──────────────┘      │
       │                                                        ▼
       │                                              ┌──────────────┐
       │                                              │ retry-30s    │  FAIL
       │                                              │ (wait 30s)   │─────┐
       │                                              └──────────────┘     │
       │                                                                    ▼
       │                                                          ┌──────────────┐
       │                                                          │ transfers.DLT│
       │                                                          │ (dead letter) │
       │                                                          └──────────────┘
       ▼
  Main partition keeps flowing!

  Permanent failure: transfers ──straight──▶ transfers.DLT
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Tiered retries with retry topics move the waiting off the main consumer so the partition keeps flowing. When a record fails transiently, it is published to a retry topic and the main consumer commits past it. The record graduates through increasing delays -- 1 second, 5 seconds, 30 seconds -- giving the failing dependency time to recover. If it still fails after the last tier, it lands in the dead letter queue.

Exponential backoff gives the dependency room to recover, and jitter spreads retries in time so a whole population of correlated failures does not stampede the dependency the moment it comes back. In front of the pipeline, failure classification gates which records enter the ladder: transient failures like timeouts are retried, permanent failures like validation errors skip straight to the DLQ.

At National Bank of India, the settlement consumer calls a credit bureau that sometimes times out. With tiered retry topics, the main partition never blocks during retries, failed records spread across the recovery window instead of stampeding, and permanently invalid records go straight to the DLT. Rajesh uses Spring Kafka's `@RetryableTopic` to auto-create the tier topics.

Remember one sentence: tiered retry topics with exponential backoff and jitter turn a flaky dependency from a partition-wide outage into a background, self-pacing recovery that protects both your throughput and the dependency itself.
